reran: cmd.sh on w4-int, w3-base and 2.13.18: identical to actual.txt; 2.12.20 (JavaConverters): BitSet.asJava.contains(null) true and LongMap(0L -> a).asJava.get(null) a. My variant on w4-int: the write side does the same, mutable.BitSet(5).asJava.add(null) adds 0 and LongMap.asJava.put(null, x) overwrites key 0, while mutable.TreeMap[Int, _] and HashMap[Int, _] store a null key in an Int-keyed map; a Java Map<Long, String> view of LongMap(0L -> zero) gives zero for get(nullLong) and getOrDefault(nullLong, d). Set[String]("a", null).asJava.contains(null) and HashMap[String, Int](null -> 1).asJava.get(null) are true and 1, as they should be.
user_impact: Java code that probes a Set<Integer> or Map<Long, V> handed over from Scala with a possibly-null boxed key, e.g. map.get(request.getId()) on a TreeMap[Long, V], LongMap, IntMap or BitSet view: it gets the entry for 0 instead of null, and remove(null) or put(null, v) changes key 0. Common Scala-side types for that are TreeMap[Long, V] and LongMap; HashMap and Map views are not affected.
fixability: design question (small): the wrapper does not know whether the element type is primitive, so the hunter's sketch (answer false, or throw, for a null argument) is wrong for Scala collections that hold null, which the wrapper must keep answering true. Options: for a null argument answer from iteration (underlying.exists(_ == null), keysIterator for maps), costing O(n) only for null probes; or type-test the underlying for the known primitive-keyed classes plus sorted collections ordered by Ordering.Int/Long. add/put of null need the same decision (NullPointerException is allowed by the contract). No binary cost.
links: HC4 (wave three, by design): same wrapper methods, cooperative == on boxed numbers, a different cause; HC3 is its Scala-side counterpart. LM7 (wave two, retronym/scala PR 540, on w4-int) adds Buffer.asJava.remove(Object) through indexOf, which answers null correctly (ArrayBuffer[Int].asJava.remove(null) is false), so it is not a duplicate; LM6 (PR 549) is the entry setValue. No scala/bug report found (scala/bug 9676 and 11894 concern nulls through converters but other methods).
note: Contract: java.util.Set.contains and Map.get/containsKey/remove may throw NullPointerException 'if the specified element is null and this set does not permit null elements (optional)', or answer false/null; true for contains(null) and the value of another key for get(null) are outside it. The unboxing is not in the wrapper's cast (asInstanceOf[A] on an erased A is a no-op) but in the Scala collection's erasure bridge: BitSet.contains(Object), LongMap.get(Object) and Ordering.Int/Long.compare(Object, Object) call BoxesRunTime.unboxToInt/unboxToLong, which maps null to 0. The hunter understated the write side (add/put of null) and its fix sketch would break null-holding collections.
